audience.programmeDescription: Pedagogical Sciences studies how children and adolescents develop within family, peer, school and wider social environments. The UvA degree combines developmental and pedagogical knowledge with research, professional skills, assessment, an internship and an empirical thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR can combine developmental, social and health psychology with research, ethics, policy and community teaching. The dedicated UvA degree provides a more sustained family- and child-focused curriculum and professional practice sequence. The options show different academic priorities; they do not establish professional registration or entry to a particular postgraduate programme.

cellNotes.text: Academic Skills A and B are compulsory in year 1. They carry no separate EC: their workload is credited within the content courses.

The normal programme requires a 6 EC internship, including approved practice or research experience, preparation, reflection and supervision. The course entry also offers a 9 EC variant; this example uses the prescribed 6 EC component. Students arrange an approved host and complete the required information and application training before starting.

Year 2 requires at least 42 first-year EC. Academic Skills C and D are compulsory with no separate EC. Testing and Measurement follows participation in Descriptive Statistics; Inferential Statistics requires passing Descriptive Statistics; Research in Practice requires passing both Descriptive Statistics and Testing and Measurement. Professional Skills 2 requires passing Professional Skills 1.

The 15 EC empirical thesis follows completion of the first two years, except that one year-2 content course and Academic Skills D may remain. At least nine colloquium points are also required for graduation: five from POW master-thesis presentations, one from a doctorate or inaugural lecture, and three from POW or Comenius lectures or conferences.

Professional Skills 3 requires passing Professional Skills 2 and following Diagnostics. Following means a recorded assessment result. It develops practical child and adolescent assessment and advice skills.

The 30 EC open space remains unspecified. Choices must not overlap the compulsory curriculum. Second- and third-year faculty courses can be selected without extra approval. First-year courses normally need to form part of a completed minor; other choices, skills and language courses require prior Examination Board approval. Exchange also requires approval.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

BENECON111.text: Explore how individuals, firms, and societies make economic decisions. This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.text: Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, measurement, sampling, surveys and experiments. Students study descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression using R and R Commander. A group project develops a research plan and instruments, collects and analyses data, and reports findings under research-ethics and privacy requirements.

BENLEAD211.name: Psychology of Leading Under Pressure
BENLEAD211.text: Examines how emotion regulation, emotional intelligence, belonging, identity safety and psychological safety shape leadership in diverse contexts, with particular attention to minority experiences. Students design and pilot a quantitative survey, collect data ethically, and use SPSS or RStudio for descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlations, group comparisons and introductory multiple regression. They interpret the findings and develop evidence-based leadership recommendations.

GOSGATE102.text: Law, Society & Justice examines legal, social and normative perspectives on law. Students compare legal traditions and study public and private law, human rights, justice, social control and change, race and gender. Case briefs, demand letters and mock trials develop legal reasoning, while a family-law topic supports the design of a socio-legal research proposal.

HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.text: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.
